correctness.rationale: Sort bundles a<=b. If the larger bundle has one good, its product ab is globally optimal. Otherwise EFX implies b-a<=min_{g in B}v_g<=b/2, so T/3<=a<=T/2, yielding ab>=2T²/9 while P*<=T²/4. Equality in both bounds forces B to have exactly two goods of value u each, A total u, and an exactly balanced global allocation requires a subbundle of A of value u/2. Conversely this is EFX and its optimum is balanced; witness (2,2,1,1) gives squared ratio 8/9. Exhaustive independent rational/integer enumeration of 456 positive-integer item multisets, 2939 EFX allocations, 4 equal cases corroborated. Strict positivity, complete allocation and two identical agents are essential.

value.rationale: The lower guarantee governs every EFX allocation (not just the existence of one selected allocation), and the equality classification determines exact welfare loss witnesses for a central fairness property. The sharp factor and rigid geometric/subset-sum mechanism are mathematically informative for the EFX–efficiency tradeoff rather than a routine restatement of EF1.
